items.q: Fill up: Delta (Δ) AG = measured AG − ______.
items.exp: Delta (Δ) AG = measured AG − normal AG. (Book p829)

items.q: Match the delta ratio to its interpretation — 1) < 1  2) 1–2  3) > 2 … A) HAGMA + metabolic alkalosis  B) HAGMA + NAGMA  C) HAGMA alone
items.exp: Delta ratio < 1: HAGMA + NAGMA; 1–2: HAGMA; > 2: HAGMA + metabolic alkalosis. (Book p829)

items.q: A patient has a HAGMA with a delta ratio of 0.6. What does this suggest?
opts: A coexisting normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
A pure HAGMA requiring no further search
An osmolal gap that must be ignored
items.exp: A delta ratio below 1 indicates HAGMA plus NAGMA, i.e. a second, normal anion gap acidosis alongside the raised gap. (Book p829)

items.q: A patient with a HAGMA has a delta ratio of 2.4. Which additional disorder does the printed table suggest?
opts: Metabolic alkalosis in addition to the HAGMA
Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis in addition to the HAGMA
No additional disorder — this is a pure HAGMA
items.exp: A delta ratio above 2 indicates HAGMA plus metabolic alkalosis. (Book p829)

items.q: Which delta ratio range corresponds to a pure high anion gap metabolic acidosis?
items.exp: Delta ratio 1–2 indicates HAGMA alone — values < 1 add NAGMA and values > 2 add metabolic alkalosis. (Book p829)

items.q: ‘The delta ratio uses the change in anion gap divided by the change in bicarbonate.’
opts: True — Delta ratio = ΔAG/ΔHCO₃⁻, with ΔAG = measured AG − normal AG
False — the delta ratio divides ΔHCO₃⁻ by ΔAG
False — the delta ratio uses the osmolal gap instead of the anion gap
True, but ΔAG is measured AG + normal AG
items.exp: Delta (Δ) AG = measured AG − normal AG, and Delta ratio = ΔAG/ΔHCO₃⁻. (Book p829)

items.q: All but one of these delta ratio interpretations are printed. Which is the odd one out?
opts: > 2 indicates HAGMA with a coexisting normal anion gap acidosis
items.exp: A ratio > 2 means HAGMA plus metabolic alkalosis; the coexisting NAGMA belongs to the < 1 range. (Book p829)
